questions.q: Why is Oracle's ROWNUM a risky direct substitute for SQL Server's TOP?
options: ROWNUM filters rows before the ORDER BY logically executes, which can produce different results than TOP with an ORDER BY
ROWNUM only works on views, never on base tables
ROWNUM is not supported in any version of Oracle
TOP and ROWNUM always return identical results with no caveats
questions.explain: This is a classic source of bugs — Oracle 12c's FETCH FIRST ROWS ONLY behaves the way SQL Server developers expect TOP to behave.

questions.q: What does a SQL Server-to-Oracle migration need to know before estimating how IDENTITY columns will be handled?
options: Which Oracle version is the target, since older Oracle needs a sequence plus a trigger while 12c+ supports GENERATED AS IDENTITY directly
Nothing — Oracle has always had an IDENTITY keyword identical to SQL Server's
Whether the table has a primary key at all
The number of rows currently in the table
questions.explain: The sequence-plus-trigger pattern and the newer GENERATED AS IDENTITY syntax represent meaningfully different amounts of migration work.

questions.q: In Oracle, what actually happens when an empty string ('') is inserted into a VARCHAR2 column?
options: Oracle stores it as NULL, since Oracle treats empty string as NULL for VARCHAR2/CHAR columns
Oracle stores it as a zero-length string identical to SQL Server's behavior
Oracle raises an error and rejects the insert in all cases
Oracle converts it to the string "NULL"
questions.explain: This is one of Oracle's best-known gotchas for SQL Server migrators, and it changes how NOT NULL constraints and equality comparisons behave.

questions.q: Why does 'WHERE MiddleName = ' '' silently return zero rows in Oracle even when rows with no middle name exist?
options: Oracle stored the empty string as NULL, and NULL never equals anything, including another NULL, so the comparison must use IS NULL instead
Oracle does not support the equals operator on string columns
MiddleName is a reserved word in Oracle
Oracle requires all WHERE clauses to use ROWNUM
questions.explain: Because '' is stored as NULL, only IS NULL will correctly match those rows in Oracle.

questions.q: How does Oracle's default handling of unquoted object identifiers differ from SQL Server's?
options: Oracle folds unquoted identifiers to uppercase by default, while SQL Server is typically case-insensitive but preserves the case as typed
Oracle and SQL Server both fold unquoted identifiers to lowercase by default
Oracle requires every identifier to be quoted, with no unquoted option
SQL Server folds unquoted identifiers to uppercase, and Oracle preserves case exactly
questions.explain: CREATE TABLE Orders and CREATE TABLE ORDERS produce the same object in Oracle, stored as ORDERS, unless the identifier is quoted.
